answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, a refundable smart-contract bond is created for each identity, locking its own commitments. This makes it costly for multiple identities to participate. Cryptographic proof is required to slash a bond, only when conflicting commitments signed for the same task are detected. Like a pigment mixing with another, a single thread can break the bond, while a quartz-like crystal structure ensures the integrity of the system.
